questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which one of these is a living thing?
questions.explanation: A kangaroo grows, eats, breathes and has babies. The others do not.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A caterpillar changes into a butterfly. In between, it rests inside a case. What is this stage called?
questions.explanation: The caterpillar turns into a butterfly inside a case called a pupa or chrysalis.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which thing do all living things do?
questions.explanation: Plants and animals all grow and make young. Plants do not walk, make sounds or eat animals.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Mia plants a bean seed. A tiny shoot pushes out of the soil. What is a young plant like this called?
questions.explanation: A small young plant that has just sprouted from a seed is called a seedling.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Fire is not a living thing, even though it needs air and seems to grow.
questions.explanation: Fire does not eat, make young or have a life cycle, so it is not alive.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Jack squeezes some wet soil. It feels sticky and he can roll it into a ball. What kind of soil is it?
questions.explanation: Clay soil is sticky when wet, so it holds together in a ball. Sand falls apart.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Farmers in Victoria grow wheat in soil. Why is soil a valuable natural resource?
choices: It is soft to walk on
Plants grow in it and give us food
questions.explanation: Plants need soil to grow. Many of our foods come from plants.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Granite is a rock used for kitchen benchtops. Which property makes it good for this job?
questions.explanation: Granite is hard and strong, so it does not scratch or break easily.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Pumice is a rock that floats on water. What does this tell us about pumice?
choices: It is as soft as chalk
It is light for its size, with tiny holes of air
questions.explanation: Pumice has many tiny holes full of air. This makes it light enough to float.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Iron ore is dug from mines in the Pilbara in Western Australia. What is iron ore used to make?
questions.explanation: Iron ore is heated to make iron and steel, which are used for buildings and cars.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which one of these is a source of heat?
questions.explanation: The Sun gives out heat and light. The other things do not make heat.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Sam leaves a metal spoon in hot soup. Soon the handle feels warm. How did the heat get to the handle?
choices: It moved from the hot soup along the spoon
It moved from the cold air into the spoon
It moved from the spoon into the soup
The spoon made its own heat
questions.explanation: Heat moves from hot things to cooler things. It travelled up the metal spoon.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A cup of hot milk at 70 degrees Celsius sits in a room at 22 degrees Celsius. What happens to the milk?
questions.explanation: Heat moves from the milk into the cooler room, so the milk cools until it matches the room.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Hot chocolate is 80 degrees Celsius. Ten minutes later it is 60 degrees Celsius. By how many degrees did it cool?
questions.explanation: 80 take away 60 is 20, so it cooled by 20 degrees.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Lily wears a woolly jumper on a cold winter day. Why does it keep her warm?
choices: It slows down heat leaving her body
It lets the cold air in
questions.explanation: Wool traps air, so her body heat escapes slowly. The jumper does not make heat.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which one of these is a liquid?
questions.explanation: Honey flows and takes the shape of its container. Sand, sugar and flour are tiny solid bits.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Ella leaves a chocolate bar in a hot car in January. It turns runny. What has happened?
choices: It melted, because heat was added
It froze, because heat was added
It melted, because heat was taken away
It froze, because heat was taken away
questions.explanation: Heat from the car made the solid chocolate melt into a liquid.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Dad puts a tray of water in the freezer. What is taken away from the water so it turns to ice?
questions.explanation: When enough heat is taken out of water, it freezes and turns into solid ice.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which sentence is true about liquids?
choices: They take the shape of their container
They always keep their own shape
questions.explanation: A liquid flows and fills the bottom of its container, so it takes its shape.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Water boils and turns into steam when it gets very hot. At how many degrees Celsius does water boil?
questions.explanation: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
